# AI Did Not Fix Your Marketing. It Made Your Mediocrity Cheaper.

Source: https://lowob.com/research/ai-made-average-marketing-cheaper/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-05-03 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Growth

> Summary: The easiest thing to do with AI is produce more, and it is the least interesting. When every company has capable models, production speed stops being an advantage; the scarce inputs become judgment, access, evidence and a point of view. A 2024 Science Advances study found AI ideas made individual stories better but made the stories more similar to one another, and B2B marketers credit AI with speed (78%) far more than quality (17%). If the input is public consensus, the output will be polished consensus.

## Key points

- AI lowers the cost of expression. It cannot manufacture a reason for an audience to care.
- In Doshi and Hauser's experiment, one AI idea raised story similarity by 10.7%; the most AI access raised rated novelty by 8.1%.
- 65% of B2B marketers faced more pressure to produce content faster in 2026; 44% credited AI with volume, 17% with quality.
- Google asks whether content offers "original information, reporting, research, or analysis" and flags "extensive automation" across many topics.
- Before publishing, ask what the piece contains that a competitor could not get by typing the same topic into the same model.

More posts. More emails. More landing pages. More summaries. More variations of the same announcement with slightly different verbs.

When every company has access to capable models, production speed stops being a meaningful advantage. The scarce inputs become judgment, access, taste, evidence and a point of view worth remembering. AI can lower the cost of expression. It cannot manufacture a reason for an audience to care.

This is why many AI-enabled content programmes feel strangely lifeless. The sentences are clean. The structure is competent. The output is technically correct. Yet nothing in the piece could only have come from that company.

## Why AI content converges

There is now direct evidence for what readers sense. Anil Doshi and Oliver Hauser ran an experiment, published in Science Advances in 2024, in which 300 writers produced short stories, some with access to AI-generated ideas, and 600 people rated them. Writers with the most AI access produced stories rated 8.1% higher for novelty. Less creative writers gained most: with five AI ideas, their stories improved by 10.7% on novelty and 11.5% on usefulness. But stories written with one AI idea were 10.7% more similar to each other than those written without.

That is the whole problem in one result. Each piece gets better. The set gets more alike. A company that adopts AI drafting improves its own average and moves closer to everyone else's.

The market pressure runs in the same direction. In the 2026 Content Marketing Institute and MarketingProfs survey of 861 B2B marketers, 65% said they had faced more pressure to produce content faster in the previous 12 months. Asked what AI contributed, 78% said speed, 59% efficiency and 44% volume; 22% said innovation and 17% quality. Among those under pressure, 35% reported burnout or creative fatigue.

| What AI changes | What it does not change |
| --- | --- |
| Cost of a draft | Cost of a reader's attention |
| Time to publish | Whether there is anything new to say |
| Quality of an individual piece | Distinctiveness of the set |
| Volume a team can ship | Evidence the team holds |

## The five symptoms of AI-mediated sameness

You can usually recognise average AI content before finishing the first paragraph.

It begins with an inflated statement about a changing landscape. It explains obvious background to an audience that already understands it. It presents five interchangeable best practices. It avoids a defensible opinion. It concludes that the future is exciting and organisations should adapt.

The problem is not that a model wrote the sentences. The problem is that the company supplied no proprietary material.

Search engines have reached the same conclusion. Google's helpful content guidance asks whether a page provides "original information, reporting, research, or analysis", and lists as a warning sign "using extensive automation to produce content on many topics". Its July 2026 guide to AI search asks for "unique expert or experienced takes that go beyond common knowledge". Content that any company could have produced is the content both readers and engines can do without.

> If the input is public consensus, the output will be polished consensus.

## The new content advantage

The strongest content systems begin with assets that cannot be generated from the public internet alone:

- direct customer conversations
- original data or structured market observations
- an operator's experience of what actually failed
- access to founders, buyers, creators and partners
- a repeatable analytical framework
- a clear belief about where the market is wrong.

AI can then help organise, compare, challenge, adapt and distribute those assets. That is a meaningful division of labour. It preserves the part that creates value and accelerates the work surrounding it.

| Humans should own | AI can accelerate |
| --- | --- |
| The thesis | Transcript analysis and theme extraction |
| Source relationships and interviews | Counterarguments to the thesis |
| Judgment and risk decisions | Outline variants and headline exploration |
| Examples and their accuracy | Channel adaptation |
| Voice and final approval | Editorial QA and archive retrieval |

Consider a founder interview. The valuable asset is not a model-generated article about "five trends in fintech". It is the founder explaining why three enterprise pilots stalled, what buyers misunderstood and what finally changed the sales process. AI can identify themes across the transcript, compare the account stories, propose a structure and produce channel variants. The substance still comes from lived commercial evidence. Our piece on the [founder interview content engine](https://lowob.com/research/founder-interview-content-engine/) sets out the method.

## The proprietary-input test

Before publishing, ask one question:

*What is present in this piece that another competent company could not produce by entering the same topic into the same model?*

If the answer is nothing, the draft is not finished. Add one or more of the following:

1. A specific observation from the market.
2. A decision framework with named variables.
3. A real example with enough detail to be useful.
4. A counterintuitive position the company can defend.
5. A tool the reader can apply immediately.

The test is cheap to run. Give the draft's title to a general-purpose model with no other context and compare the two. Whatever survives in yours and is missing from the model's is the proprietary content. If very little survives, that is the finding. Our piece on [content with a job](https://lowob.com/research/content-with-a-job/) adds the other half of the brief: who reads it and what they decide.

## Build a point-of-view ledger

Most companies maintain a content calendar. Fewer maintain a record of what they actually believe.

Create a point-of-view ledger with five fields:

| Field | Question it answers |
| --- | --- |
| Market belief | What do we think is changing? |
| Consensus view | What does the market normally say? |
| Our disagreement | Where do we see it differently? |
| Evidence | What have we observed that supports the position? |
| Implication | What should a founder or buyer do differently? |

This ledger should feed the content calendar. Without it, the team is scheduling formats before identifying ideas. Each entry is a small [decision record](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-decision-record/): it has an owner, a date and evidence, and it can be revised when the evidence changes. Over a year, the ledger shows which positions held and which did not, which is itself content no competitor can copy.

## Measure recognition, not production

AI makes word count and post frequency easier to inflate, which makes them even less useful as measures of quality. Look instead for signals of recognition and consequence.

| Signal | How to record it |
| --- | --- |
| The right people share the piece with their own commentary | Log shares by named target accounts and partners |
| Prospects repeat the framing in sales conversations | Tag call notes where a buyer uses the firm's language |
| Partners ask the team to brief them on the topic | Count inbound briefing requests per quarter |
| Readers save templates or return to related pieces | Downloads and return visits on tool pages |
| The content creates qualified conversations | First meetings where the buyer cites a piece |

The goal is not to prove that the company can publish every day. The goal is to become associated with a valuable way of seeing the market. Our piece [Thought leadership that sales can use](https://lowob.com/research/thought-leadership-that-sales-can-use/) covers how to turn that association into pipeline.

AI is an extraordinary production and analysis layer. But when it is used to avoid the harder work of developing judgment, it allows a company to become forgettable at higher speed. The AI content advantage is not more content. It is extracting more value from insight that only your company can provide.

## lowob takeaways

- **Better pieces, more alike.** AI raises individual quality and lowers collective distinctiveness.
- **Supply proprietary material.** Conversations, data, failures and a stated disagreement with consensus.
- **Run the proprietary-input test.** Compare the draft with what a bare model produces from the title.
- **Keep a point-of-view ledger.** Beliefs, evidence and implications feed the calendar, not the reverse.

## Common questions

### Why does AI-generated marketing content all sound the same?

Models produce the most likely text from the input they are given. If the input is public consensus, the output converges. A 2024 study found AI ideas made stories 10.7% more similar to each other.

### Does Google penalise AI-generated content?

Google targets content made primarily to manipulate rankings, including mass-produced pages, whoever or whatever wrote it. Its guidance rewards original information, research or analysis and flags extensive automation across many topics.

### How do you make AI content stand out?

Feed it material competitors do not have: customer conversations, original data, operator experience and a defensible position. Then test whether the draft contains anything a bare model would not produce from the same title.

### What is a point-of-view ledger?

A record of what the company believes is changing, the consensus view, where it disagrees, the evidence, and what a buyer should do differently. It feeds the content calendar.
